title: Your Water Heater Is Probably Set Too Hot #shorts
keys: 120 140 six seconds burn landlord cover sediment quart three months follow too hot five

segments.text: Your water heater might be set too hot, and that's a burn risk.
At a hundred forty degrees, hot water can cause a serious burn in about six seconds. At a hundred twenty, it takes about five minutes.

segments.label: RECOMMENDED
segments.text: That's why the Department of Energy and the Consumer Product Safety Commission both recommend a hundred twenty.
On many gas tanks, it's the knob near the bottom. If the dial is behind a metal cover, leave it to your landlord or a pro.
Bonus tip. The Department of Energy says draining about a quart every three months clears sediment that makes the heater less efficient. Ask your landlord who handles it.
